::: {.why}
Every model this week beyond Black-Scholes prices by simulation, and a technique that cuts the standard error by a factor of ten for almost no extra code is worth an hour once.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement antithetic variates and a control variate, and report the variance reduction factor for each.
- Say which technique works when, and why a control variate needs a correlated instrument with a known price.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement both in qlib/derivatives/mc.py: antithetic paths, and a control variate using the underlying's terminal value or a Black-Scholes-priced option whose value you know exactly. Report the standard error with and without each, and the effective speedup in paths.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Apply it to something without a closed form: price a path-dependent option, such as an Asian or a barrier, under Heston, using the geometric-average Asian's closed form as a control variate. That combination is the standard trick and it is worth having implemented once.
:::
:::
